unit_rule: A unit is a distinct rule or a contiguous operational block. Split compound rules with different comparisons. Keep repeated rules in different documents as occurrences. Directions describe the stated comparison, not net welfare or independent legal violations.

units.title: Instruction to follow Regulation E
units.assessment: Introduces the governing rule and the liability instructions assessed separately below.

units.title: Two-day clock starts at statement
units.assessment: The text incorrectly starts the two-business-day clock at the statement rather than learning of device loss or theft. It can move a prompt reporter into a higher tier or extend the lower tier after earlier discovery. We record the definite clock error as directionally unclear.

units.title: Flat $500 tier within 60 days
units.assessment: The $500 ceiling depends on delayed notice after learning of device loss, the timing of later transfers, and the bank establishing preventability. Statement age alone does not establish $500 liability.

units.title: Unlimited liability after 60 days
units.assessment: The statement-notice rule concerns subsequent preventable transfers after the 60-day period, not automatic unlimited liability for the original transfer.

units.title: Dispute earliest duplicate
units.assessment: The bank may use one filing to represent a duplicate-charge error. Without knowing what one filing covers, transaction selection alone does not establish weaker protection.

units.title: Verify customer
units.assessment: Identifying the consumer and account is legitimate. The clause alone specifies no unlawful evidentiary barrier.

units.title: Minimum disputed amount of $1
units.assessment: The error-resolution duty has no $1 minimum for a covered error after qualifying notice.

units.title: Transaction-age deadline
units.assessment: The notice period runs from sending the statement that first shows the error, rather than from the transaction date.

units.title: Open-dispute cap by account tier
units.assessment: The investigation duty for a properly reported covered error does not depend on the number of other disputes.

units.title: Open account required to file
units.assessment: The bank must handle a properly asserted error even after the account closes.

units.title: Identify ATM operator
units.assessment: Routing an investigation by ATM operator is not itself a denial of an error-resolution right.

units.title: Tool identifiers and classification fields
units.assessment: These fields describe the interface and its taxonomy. The labels do not themselves establish authorization. We test the lost-wallet reference classification separately.

units.title: Merchant-contact field for non-fraud claims
units.assessment: The wording can mean an obligatory question or prior merchant contact. Asking is permissible. Making investigation depend on the answer would restrict rights. Document 032 states the credit exclusion expressly.

units.title: Recommend a police report
units.legal_pinpoint: Comment 11(b)(1)-2; CFPB EFT FAQ Error Resolution 4
units.assessment: This clause recommends a report and does not expressly make it a condition of investigation. The separate customer-facing document 036 uses stronger language.

units.title: Written statement and consent to use conversation
units.assessment: A bank may request written confirmation, but the rule requires notice of the requirement and time to respond. Accepting the conversation reduces burden. The blanket eligibility wording omits the timing conditions, so we do not assign one direction.

units.title: Credit cross-reference and card actions
units.assessment: The credit cross-reference points to document 032, whose rules we assess separately. Card freezing, replacement, and action precedence are security procedures without an independent legal threshold here.

units.title: Conditional provisional-credit duty
units.assessment: The law requires temporary credit when the bank uses the extended investigation period, subject to exceptions.

units.title: Standard credit deadline
units.assessment: Ten business days is the standard deadline. We read this line with the conditions introduced in the document, rather than as a promise of credit after an already completed investigation.

units.title: New-account credit deadline
units.assessment: Twenty business days can apply, but the legal trigger is a transfer within 30 days after the first deposit. The guide substitutes an account-opening age without specifying when to measure it. Depending on interpretation it can shorten the available period. We leave the direction unclear because the relevant measurement date is unstated.

units.title: Statement-based reporting window
units.assessment: The clause uses the statement date. The law uses transmittal of the first statement showing the error and has a documentation-request extension. Direction depends on which date the bank stores.

units.title: Listed eligible error categories
units.assessment: These categories can qualify. This unit records the affirmative inclusions. We assess omissions and categorical exclusions separately.

units.title: Written confirmation prerequisite
units.assessment: A failure to supply requested confirmation within ten business days can excuse temporary credit. The clause omits the request, notice, and waiting-period predicates.

units.title: Open account without holds required for credit
units.assessment: Closed status or a hold is not a categorical exception to the error-resolution or conditional temporary-credit duty.

units.title: Goods or services not received
units.assessment: A merchant-performance complaint alone need not allege an electronic-transfer error. The exclusion is consistent only on that narrow reading, not when the customer also alleges a covered error.

units.title: Recurring charge after cancellation excluded
units.assessment: A post-cancellation charge can involve an unauthorized or incorrect transfer. Its category alone cannot eliminate the conditional credit duty.

units.title: ATM deposits and incorrect amounts excluded
units.assessment: Both categories can contain covered errors. The categorical exclusion removes the conditional credit duty.

units.title: Merchant contact required for credit
units.assessment: Prior merchant contact is not one of the exceptions to the conditional temporary-credit duty for covered errors.

units.title: Shared PIN removes credit requirement
units.assessment: Sharing a PIN does not by itself resolve authority for the disputed transfer. This categorical exclusion is broader than the rule for a person whom the consumer actually authorizes.

units.title: New-account online claims excluded
units.assessment: New accounts can receive longer deadlines. Combining a new account with a card-not-present transaction does not create a blanket credit exemption.

units.title: Full amount of temporary credit
units.assessment: The rule generally requires the alleged error amount plus interest where applicable. The text omits interest and introduces offsets in the next line. Its comparison with credit-card policy is outside this Regulation E audit.

units.title: Deduct $50 or $500 from temporary credit
units.assessment: The provision permits withholding at most $50, with specified predicates. A $500 liability offset exceeds that allowance even when ultimate liability might reach $500.

units.title: 45 business days to investigate
units.assessment: The ordinary extended period is 45 calendar days. Business days give the bank longer.

units.title: 90-day extensions omit domestic POS
units.assessment: The policy lists foreign transactions, foreign merchant POS, and new accounts, leaving domestic POS under its shorter default. The law also permits 90 days for domestic POS. This benefit concerns that omitted extension, not the separate business-day error.

units.title: Reverse credit when no error found
units.assessment: The law allows a reversal after the required investigation and notices. This clause alone does not supply the omitted post-reversal payment protection.

units.title: Three-business-day advance notice of reversal
units.assessment: The ordinary rule allows notice upon debiting and protects specified payments for five business days. The bank promises earlier warning. That promise does not replace the separate five-day protection, which the document omits.

units.title: Access to supporting documents
units.assessment: After an adverse finding the customer may request the documents on which the bank relied.

units.title: Electronic-transfer coverage
units.assessment: The listed transfer types can fall within Regulation E for covered consumer accounts. General coverage still has statutory exceptions.

units.title: Liability tiers without clock anchors
units.assessment: The summary gives three amounts but omits the distinct discovery and statement clocks. It cannot determine liability without facts and conditions not stated here.

units.title: Right to dispute listed errors
units.assessment: The listed unauthorized transfers, incorrect amounts, omissions, and bookkeeping errors correspond to covered types, assuming an electronic transfer and qualifying notice.

units.title: Prompt investigation
units.assessment: The ordinary investigation deadline is ten business days, with the stated statutory extensions available.

units.title: Report results within three business days
units.assessment: The deadline matches the rule after completing the investigation.

units.title: Correct error within one business day
units.assessment: The deadline matches the rule after determining that an error occurred.

units.title: Credit during an extended investigation
units.assessment: This accurately states the ordinary ten-business-day procedure for qualifying disputes. The new-account extension appears in document 032.

units.title: Written confirmation of every resolution
units.assessment: The law generally permits oral notice unless it specifies otherwise. The policy promises writing even for favorable resolutions. Written adverse findings are already mandatory.

units.title: Copies of investigation documents
units.assessment: The law expressly provides this right after an adverse or different-error finding. The policy states it without qualification, potentially broadening access but leaving the intended scope unclear.

units.title: Advance notice before reversal
units.assessment: This repeats the advance-warning benefit in document 032. It is a second occurrence of the same benefit, not an independent type of protection.

units.title: How to report and scope reminders
units.assessment: Reporting promptly, describing the transaction, following a confirmation request, and keeping records are practical advice. Personal-account coverage and separate credit-card rules are broad reminders rather than new thresholds.

units.title: Lost-card and stolen-card security protocols
units.assessment: Decline-code diagnosis, verification, replacement, and escalation prescribe security workflow. They make no independently testable claim about liability or error-resolution time limits here.

units.title: Balance explanations and diagnostic steps
units.assessment: Explains holds, pending transactions, balance checks, and settings. These are operational context, not independent assertions about the statutory opt-in threshold.

units.title: Opt-in required for overdraft coverage
units.assessment: Regulation E conditions fees for ATM and one-time debit-card overdrafts on opt-in. It permits fee-free payment without opt-in. The policy conflates payment with charging and does not establish a single directional consumer effect.

units.title: Overdraft options and closed-card handling
units.assessment: The steps offer explanations, transfers, and account checks. The law does not require the bank to pay an overdraft. Closing a card after account closure differs from refusing a dispute about a past transfer.

classification_rule: First separate context and operational blocks. For substantive comparisons, use unclear when the trigger, scope, or direction cannot be fixed from the wording, including bidirectional clock changes and omitted predicates. Use less protection for an explicit exclusion, added barrier, or excessive amount/deadline under a stated covered condition. Use more protection for an explicit additional promise or shorter available investigation period under the stated reading. Use consistent for a rule that matches on the documented scope. A benefit does not excuse a different missing duty. Never infer direction solely from an omitted detail.
